title: GFS Augments Photonics Portfolio: Will SMART Partnership Boost Growth?
author: Zacks.Com
description: GlobalFoundries (GFS) has partnered with SMART Photonics to combine silicon and indium phosphide photonics manufacturing capabilities. The company reported 62% year-over-year revenue growth in communications infrastructure and data center in Q2 2026, driven by strong AI and optical networking demand. GFS is advancing 1.6-terabit and 3.2-terabit optical modules while producing 200-gigabit-per-lane technology, though financial contributions from the SMART partnership will take time to materialize.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong 62% YoY revenue growth in communications infrastructure for seven consecutive quarters of double-digit growth, strategic partnership with SMART Photonics to expand photonics capabilities, and advancing next-generation optical modules position the company well in the growing AI and data center markets.
Record Q2 2026 revenue of $460 million (24% YoY growth) with silicon photonics business achieving triple-digit growth and $680 million annualized revenue run rate, demonstrating strong market demand.
Fiscal Q4 2026 revenue of $2.05 billion (34% YoY growth) with non-GAAP gross margin expanding to 40.2%, indicating strong performance in the optical-connectivity market.

title: GlobalFoundries Drives Gross Margin Expansion: Can the Momentum Last?
author: Zacks.Com
description: GlobalFoundries reported strong Q2 2026 results with gross profit rising 24% to $505M and IFRS gross margin expanding to 28.3%. The company is benefiting from favorable business mix, manufacturing productivity gains, and strong demand in communications infrastructure and data centers, which surged 62% year-over-year. However, sustaining this momentum will require balancing profitability with investments in future growth and continued movement toward higher-value technologies.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong Q2 2026 results with 24% gross profit growth, expanding margins (28.3% IFRS, 29.9% Non-IFRS), and robust demand in high-margin segments like communications infrastructure (62% YoY growth). Stock up 44.1% over the past year. However, rated Hold (Rank #3) due to valuation concerns and execution risks.
Gross margin improved to 32.5% in Q2 2026 from 29.2% in Q1, driven by higher wafer shipments and better capacity utilization, demonstrating competitive strength in the foundry sector.

Achieved exceptional gross margin of 67.7% in Q2 2026, up 150 basis points sequentially and 910 basis points year-over-year, driven by cost-improvement initiatives and higher capacity utilization, demonstrating industry leadership.

title: Can GFS' Marvell Deal for SiGe Capacity Expansion Accelerate Growth?
author: Zacks.Com
description: GlobalFoundries has signed a multi-year agreement with Marvell Technology to expand silicon germanium (SiGe) production capacity at its Burlington, Vermont facility. The expansion will support next-generation optical transceivers and networking solutions for AI and cloud data centers. GFS shares have outperformed the industry over the past year, though the company faces competition from UMC and TSMC in the optical connectivity market.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: The company secured a multi-year agreement with Marvell to expand SiGe production capacity, positioning it to capitalize on growing AI and cloud infrastructure demand. Stock has outperformed the industry by 9% over the past year, and earnings estimates have increased for both 2026 and 2027.

Marvell secured a strategic multi-year supply agreement with GlobalFoundries to support its optical connectivity solutions for AI and cloud networks, indicating strong demand for its products and secure supply chain planning.

UMC is advancing in silicon photonics and high-speed optical connectivity capabilities, competing directly with GFS. While making progress, the article presents this as competitive pressure rather than a standout achievement.

TSMC is strengthening its silicon photonics and CoWoS packaging capabilities for AI data centers, positioning it as a competitor to GFS. The company is advancing but not highlighted as gaining significant advantage in this specific market segment.

title: GFS Gains From Expanding Partner base: Will it Boost Growth Prospects?
author: Zacks.Com
description: GlobalFoundries is expanding its semiconductor partnerships across AI, optical networking, automotive, and quantum technologies. Recent deals include a long-term manufacturing agreement with Monolithic Power Systems and $375 million in R&D funding from the U.S. Department of Commerce for quantum semiconductors. The company also partnered with RAAAM Memory Technologies on power-efficient memory solutions. However, GFS stock has underperformed the industry by 33.6% over the past year and trades at a higher valuation than peers, with a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: While GFS is expanding partnerships and securing significant R&D funding ($375M), indicating positive strategic developments, the company's stock has significantly underperformed the industry (-33.6% vs +24.4%), trades at premium valuation (17.65 vs 12.79 industry average), and carries a Hold rating. Growth prospects depend on successful commercialization and customer adoption, creating uncertainty.

UMC is actively expanding manufacturing capacity in Singapore and Taiwan to address rising demand, demonstrating competitive positioning. However, the article presents this as competitive pressure on GFS rather than highlighting UMC's independent strengths.

TSMC is described as a 'much larger and more technologically broad competitor' with advantages in offering an integrated manufacturing ecosystem. Recent collaboration with ASML on advanced lithography technology demonstrates technological leadership and competitive strength.

Monolithic Power Systems secured a long-term manufacturing agreement with GFS to deploy proprietary technology targeting high-growth markets including automotive, robotics, and AI infrastructure, indicating strong business expansion.

title: Why D-Wave Quantum Stock Popped Today
author: Rich Smith
description: D-Wave Quantum received up to $100 million in funding from the U.S. Department of Commerce under the CHIPS and Science Act, causing its stock to rise 10.86%. However, the government also awarded similar $100 million grants to rival quantum companies Quantinuum and Rigetti Computing. GlobalFoundries received the largest award at $375 million, suggesting it may be the government's preferred champion rather than D-Wave.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Stock popped 10.86% on announcement of $100 million government funding to scale and commercialize quantum capabilities, though the positive impact is tempered by the fact that competitors received equal awards.
Stock up 7.20% after receiving $100 million CHIPS Act award, demonstrating investor confidence in the company's quantum computing prospects.
